hypothesis: The compact-refine decompose (61b1f3b, 20260928-070500) measured the compaction_start frame QUEUED at command dispatch (+0.2ms) but ARRIVING at the client +48.2ms p50 at stock-10MiB: the pre-summarizer CPU phases (digest capture + cut scan + token estimation + details/aux resolution ~= 46ms) run without an executor yield, so the RPC LineWriter's writer task cannot flush the queued frame until the pipeline's first true await (the aux spawn_blocking join). The lane: reproduce the delay at the tip on both client surfaces (headless RPC + the kitty TUI), locate the non-yielding span, implement the parity-safe fix (a bounded writer flush between the compaction_start emit and the pipeline), prove the frozen surfaces byte-identical, and pair-measure the visibility metric. Honest negative if the TUI surface shows no starvation (the decompose record's '(TUI included)' parenthetical was an inference, not a measurement).
source_finding: bench 61b1f3b event_visibility_flush_starvation: 'the compaction_start event frame is QUEUED at command dispatch (~+0.2ms) but ARRIVES at the client +48.2ms p50 (n=8, stock-10MiB) - the pre-summarizer CPU phases run without an await point on the async runtime, so the LineWriter writer task cannot flush the queued frame until the pipeline's first await'; candidates_reported_only #2: 'COMPACT EVENT-VISIBILITY (+46ms at 10MiB)'
approach: (1) CODE DECOMPOSE at the tip e2ee82f2d: the RPC mode hosts the session in-process on the CLI's multi-thread runtime; rpc/commands.rs compact queues compaction_start through LineWriter (mpsc -> one writer task) then enters engine.session.compact() whose pre-summarizer span (harness_digest_inputs -> recent_message_texts/session.lock all Ready-fast-path, prepare_compaction cut scan, context_tokens, details_for) has NO true executor yield until the aux spawn_blocking join - the mpsc send wakes the writer task into the busy worker's LIFO slot (tokio: not stealable), so the frame waits the span out. print mode emits directly (println at the emit - no starvation); the daemon worker path (the TUI) emits CompactionStart BEFORE the pipeline and the pipeline runs on the engine's PRIVATE runtime (block_on from spawn_blocking) while the event fan-out rides the worker runtime - architecturally not starved. (2) BASELINE FIRST at the tip (base binary sha ae1b2a1b33256abc, VM yyovso7v3awsm7ojgu2bfi1l 16c/32GB ubuntu:22.04 rustup 1.98.1): the decompose harness replicated verbatim (cvis_probe.py: arrival-accurate frame pump, fresh agent dir/home/tmp per trial, models.json -> offline mock prime-inference/mock-1, per-trial fixture prehash, quiet gate, zombie sweep): cs (compaction_start client-arrival) p50 +51.80ms n=8 stock-10MiB (the record's +48.2ms reproduced; ce p50 +136.46 = the command wall, start->end gap 84.1ms - the frame strands behind the first-yield point); the 256KiB control cs p50 +1.14ms n=6 (the size-scaling of the CPU span). (3) CANDIDATE: both RPC emit sites (the direct compact command handler + the prompt-admitted /compact) await a bounded LineWriter drain (drain_within, COMPACT_FRAME_FLUSH_BUDGET 50ms) right after queueing compaction_start, before the pipeline; the budget keeps a stalled reader (a full pipe) from wedging the compaction (TS never blocks a command on the reader). (4) PAIRED ABBA same-VM sequential, sha-asserted unlink-then-copy binary swaps (base ae1b2a1b33 / cand 0f2f85f4d), I/O advisory v1.0 preflights at every leg boundary (PHASE MODEL, re-classified per boundary; NO-CEILING), blocks A/B/B/A stock x4 + small x3 + the pristine-fixture stock rerun R1..R4. (5) TUI legs: the tui-typing lane's PTYSession protocol (TUI --offline --resume 10MiB over the daemon worker, per-trial HOME/agent-dir/socket, settings patched: no allowedModels + auto-compaction disabled so the loader is the MANUAL /compact's), typed /compact (30ms inter-key), the chunk-ledger first-byte search for the loader label 'Compacting context', ABBA T1..T4 x3. (6) TS ANCHOR: official TS 0.9.6 (vendored install, in-place exec) under the SAME driver/mock/fixture, n=4. (7) ORACLES: two in-tree e2e served-path tests (the start frame must arrive inside the flush budget AND after it the pipeline must span the stranding window - the anti-vacuity side; plus the stalled-reader bound: get_messages fills the 64KB pipe for real, the compaction must run BEHIND the stall - the durable row lands while no reader drains, which bites against an unbounded drain), per-trial frame-stream byte-identity across arms, compaction-row identity, and the rpc_mode_e2e suite regression.
parity_notes: Frozen surfaces untouched and ORACLE-PROVEN: the RPC frame streams are byte-identical across arms per trial (16/16 stock + 6/6 small, normalized only for per-trial session ids/paths/timestamps - the compaction_start/compaction_end shapes, the CompactionResult, and every response byte identical); the compaction row (summary, details, tokensBefore, firstKeptEntryId) identical across arms on both fixtures; response success all trials; session-JSONL rows identical modulo the kernel ipython_state notice row whose presence is kernel-boot-dependent WITHIN arms (7396-7398 stock, 194-195 small - disclosed). RLM wire, prompts, TUI output bytes: untouched (the change is a timing-only flush inside the RPC stdio transport; the TUI surface is not on the changed path). THE TIMING PARITY STORY (measured, not assumed): TS 0.9.6 ITSELF strands the frame (+187.47ms p50 n=4, its own pre-summarizer CPU behind Node's async stdout write) - the Rust base (+48.80ms) is not a timing divergence from TS, and the candidate (+0.143ms) is a strict improvement over BOTH; the PR claim is the client-visibility improvement with TS's own delay disclosed as the anchor. The fix adds one bounded await (<=50ms, normally ~0.2ms) to the compact handler; against a fully stalled reader the compact proceeds after the budget (the unbounded-drain class would wedge - the stalled-reader oracle bites on exactly that).
